<reason>A narrowly wins on the five-year requirement. B made the stronger general case for targeted transfers and effectively challenged the claim that broad coverage eliminates savings. But A offered withdrawal conditional on demonstrated delivery and exposed why scheduling price increases does not establish payment capacity. B’s emergency-enrollment response insufficiently justified completing removal despite substantial exclusion. A’s overstated fiscal claims and clipped speeches keep the margin small.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>After B explicitly maintained year-five removal despite missed households, A distinguished the readily executable price increase from the harder promise of reliable payments. B’s reply that subsidies also provide uncertain protection was important, but did not resolve why a fixed deadline beats readiness-based withdrawal in low-capacity states.</best_rebuttal>
